newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest milling wheat soars in record turnover.
newsitem.headline: Budapest milling wheat soars in record turnover.

text.p: Hungary's milling wheat futures prices continued to soar on Wednesday fuelled by concerns over crop quality and expectations of a rise in demand in Poland after floods, traders said.
"Milling wheat is going up massively as the Hungarian market continues to believe that the recent heavy rains harmed the quality of the crop," said Robert Vajo of Termin Broker.
Grains turnover rocketed to the highest daily figure this year at 1.668 billion forints, up from Tuesday's one billion forints.
Milling wheat deals represented some 90 percent of the volume of 3,174 lots, which rose from Tuesday's 2,012.
Milling wheat futures, freed up on Tuesday after three days of limit rises, firmed 400 to 1,480 forints on Wednesday, rising almost as quickly as on Tuesday.
The August price settled at 25,070 forints per tonne and September at 26,030, both up 1,170 forints, December finished 1,480 higher at 27,800 and May firmed 1,170 forints to end at 28,630.

Poland may need imports after its milling wheat crops were devastated by floods, traders said, adding that continuing rains and crop uncertainties in Poland, France and Germany were likely to boost milling wheat further.
The market will have a clearer picture on crops by the second half of August, they added.
Corn futures, boosted recently by the rainy weather which was believed to improve the crop, closed mixed on Thursday with more stable prices projected, traders said.
"If the crop outlook and international prices do not change, no substantial move in corn prices can be expected," Vajo said.
Feed wheat prices were also seen stabilising after recent falls, traders said, adding that the December and March positions rose on Wednesday.
December feed wheat closed at 19,050 forints, up 150, while March gained 400 forints, to finish at 19,800.
